idea-plugin.name: Keymap Manager
idea-plugin.description:
Manage your JetBrains keymaps and resolve keyboard-shortcut conflicts on macOS. Open it from Tools → Keymap Manager… or Find Action.

What it does
  • Find conflicts — a live, grouped report of every shortcut that clashes with a macOS system shortcut (read from the JetBrains Runtime's live system-shortcut table, the same source as the IDE's own conflict banner), plus double-bound keys (one keystroke on several actions) and a separate section for macOS overlaps the IDE doesn't flag. Each conflict is explained — whether your IDE still wins the key or macOS takes it first — with tailored advice.
  • Fix in place — rebind or remove a shortcut straight from the report. The rebind field captures a real keypress (even IDE-bound combos) and supports German keys (Ä Ö Ü ß), with a live green/red check for macOS overlaps and existing bindings.
  • Manage keymaps — pick any installed keymap, then activate, duplicate, rename or delete it.
  • Import / export keymaps as XML — the whole inheritance chain, or selected categories (conflicts, overlaps, double-bound keys, or just your changes versus the parent keymap).
Bundled keymap — includes MacBook Pro DE, a macOS keymap tuned for MacBook Pro keyboards with the German (T1) layout, avoiding shortcuts that are physically unpressable there (keys like / = ; ' ` [ ] are only Shift/Option chords, and there is no numpad or Insert key). Select it under Settings → Keymap.

macOS-focused. Report wording adapts to the host IDE (IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand, Android Studio, …).

Source code: github.com/stefan-huettemann/keymap-manager
idea-plugin.change-notes:
• Conflict report with per-conflict advice, in-place rebind/remove, and XML export.
  • Import a keymap from XML (gear menu → Import…): validates the file, resolves a name clash, and lets you pick a parent when the file's declared parent isn't installed. Imported keymaps can be deleted again.
  • Bundled MacBook Pro DE keymap for the German (T1) MacBook Pro layout.
  • Report wording adapts to the host IDE (IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, GoLand, Android Studio, …).
